Little by little, things began to change. Tom always says that small steps matter more than big plans. People around Nina often share different ideas about the temple fair. What's more, vesak lanterns soften the temple dusk.

The moon-lit yard has become an important part of daily life. Nina keeps a small bird at home and feeds it every morning. At first, Nina found it difficult to keep the habit. What's more, a hearty stew waited in the bothy.

Nina bought a pair of shoes online because it was much cheaper. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Nina is saving money to buy a ticket to Chengdu. Braise the ribs in cider for three hours.

The temple fair looked quieter than usual that evening. On Wednesday evenings, Nina reviews the notes from class. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The yule log serves twelve.
Nina believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. The experience taught Nina more than any book could.
